entries.name: Martin Luther King Jr.

expected.sentence:
King and Abernathy returned to serve five-day contempt sentences after their Supreme Court appeal failed; admitted October 30, 1967. The five-day term is confirmed; the November 4 release is calculated from the sentence (no original discharge record located).

Verdict as recorded: Yes — affirmed by the U.S. Supreme Court, 5-4 (1967)

Charges as recorded: Criminal contempt — for the 1963 Birmingham marches in defiance of the anti-demonstration injunction (Walker v. City of Birmingham)

updates.sentence: Five days in jail and a $50 fine for contempt, upheld on appeal. Taken into custody at Birmingham airport October 30, 1967 and held in Jefferson County Jail. Released early on November 3, 1967, before a planned vigil, by Judge William Barber; the actual custody interval was shorter than the five-day sentence.

entries.rationale: October 31, 1967 AP report says all four ministers were arrested Monday afternoon upon landing at Birmingham airport. Southern Courier November 11-12, 1967 p1 reports all four released the previous Friday, November 3, early before the planned vigil, after less than four days. November 4 is not the actual release. Preserve unrelated cases and biographies.
